description:

title: P0: Green Build Integrity - switch CI to npm ci and lock legacy-peer-deps
description:
All three CI workflows (build, nightly, release) use npm install --legacy-peer-deps instead of npm ci --legacy-peer-deps. npm install is non-deterministic and can resolve different package versions than the lockfile, which caused the dompurify test failure.

Fix: Add .npmrc with legacy-peer-deps=true and switch all Install Dependencies steps to npm ci.

Acceptance: npm ci succeeds locally; CI uses deterministic installs from lockfile.
close_reason: Added .npmrc with legacy-peer-deps=true, regenerated lockfile to sync @emnapi/runtime, switched all three CI workflows to npm ci for deterministic installs. npm ci and all 620 tests pass.

title: P0: Secure IPC/File Access - path guard and shell:openExternal allowlist
description:
Implement project-root path guard for all fs:* IPC handlers in electron.js to prevent path traversal and arbitrary host-path access. Add protocol+hostname allowlist validation for shell:openExternal. Add tests.

Why: Without path guards, a compromised renderer (e.g. via XSS in .rpy content) can use fs:writeFile/removeEntry/etc to read/write/delete arbitrary files anywhere on the host. shell:openExternal with no URL validation can open file: or javascript: URLs.

Acceptance: Security tests pass; fs:* IPC no longer allows arbitrary host-path access; shell:openExternal only allows https:/http: protocols.
close_reason: Implemented project-root path guard for all fs:* IPC handlers, shell:openExternal URL allowlist, and 19 passing security tests

title: P1 - Coverage gate for risky code paths
description:
The project has 620 unit tests but no enforced coverage thresholds. Several high-risk modules — the Ren'Py parser/analysis worker, file-system IPC manager, markdown sanitization, and canvas interaction logic — have little or no direct test coverage. Before 1.0, we need minimum thresholds defined and enforced in CI for these modules so regressions in critical paths are caught.

## Why

Coverage thresholds do not guarantee correctness, but they prevent the silent erosion of test coverage on the modules where bugs have the highest impact (data loss via bad file I/O, XSS via unsanitized markdown, parser errors causing incorrect canvas state). Enforcing thresholds in CI makes this durable.

## What to do

**Define targets (start conservative — achievable, not aspirational)**
Agree on per-module statement coverage minimums for:
- src/workers/renpyAnalysis.worker.ts (parser + analysis) — suggested 60%
- src/lib/ipcSecurity.js (already well-tested) — suggested 90%
- Markdown sanitization path (wherever marked/DOMPurify is called) — suggested 70%
- Key canvas interaction logic (pointer event handlers in StoryCanvas, RouteCanvas, ChoiceCanvas) — suggested 40% (canvas interaction is hard to unit test; set a floor, not a ceiling)

**Add/expand tests**
For each module below its threshold, add targeted tests until the threshold is met:
- Parser/analysis: edge cases in label detection, jump/call resolution, route link generation
- File-system manager: IPC handler behavior for missing files, permission errors, path edge cases
- Markdown sanitization: confirm XSS vectors are stripped, confirm valid markdown renders
- Canvas logic: pointer event sequences for drag, selection, and group operations

**Enforce in CI**
- Configure Vitest coverage (v8 or istanbul) with per-file or per-module thresholds in vitest.config.ts
- Add coverage run to the build.yml CI job so threshold violations fail the build

## What NOT to do

- Do not chase 100% coverage — set achievable minimums on risky paths only
- Do not add tests for trivial getters, pure UI rendering, or already-covered modules
- Do not block nightly on coverage — only the build/release CI path

## Acceptance

- vitest.config.ts defines coverage thresholds for the 4 agreed modules
- npm test (with coverage) passes all thresholds locally
- build.yml enforces coverage and fails on threshold regression
acceptance_criteria: Coverage thresholds defined and enforced in CI; npm test with coverage passes all thresholds

title: P1 - Critical E2E Smoke Suite (Playwright)
description:
The project has no end-to-end tests. Before 1.0, we need a minimal smoke suite that catches regressions in the most critical user flows and can gate the release workflow in CI.

## Why

Unit and component tests (currently 620) verify logic in isolation but cannot catch integration failures — broken IPC, file I/O regressions, game-runner state, or navigation flows that span multiple components. A small Playwright suite closing these gaps is a release-readiness requirement.

## What to do

**Setup**
- Install and configure Playwright for Electron (use playwright + electron or @playwright/test with the Electron launch adapter)
- Add playwright.config.ts targeting the built Electron app
- Add npm scripts: test:e2e (run suite) and test:e2e:ci (headless, for CI)

**Smoke tests (minimum required)**
1. Open existing project — launch app, open a .rpy project via dialog mock or CLI arg, verify canvas renders at least one block
2. Edit + save + reload — modify block content in Monaco editor, save (Ctrl+S), simulate reload, verify content persists
3. Run game + stop game — click Run, verify game-running state indicators appear, click Stop, verify idle state returns
4. Warp-to-label flow — open warp modal, select a label, verify warp command is issued to Ren'Py
5. Diagnostics panel clickthrough — open diagnostics panel, click a diagnostic entry, verify the correct block/tab becomes active

**CI integration**
- Add e2e job to release.yml that runs test:e2e:ci
- Gate release tag workflow on smoke suite pass
- Smoke suite does NOT need to run on every push — release tags only is acceptable

## What NOT to do

- Do not build a comprehensive regression suite — 5 smoke tests is the target
- Do not test UI appearance/styling — behavioral flows only
- Do not block the nightly or build workflows on E2E (release tags only)

## Acceptance

- All 5 smoke tests pass locally against a built Electron app
- release.yml e2e job runs and passes for release tags
- Existing unit test suite (620 tests) still passes
acceptance_criteria: 5 smoke tests pass locally and in release CI; unit suite unaffected

title: App.tsx lint hygiene: remove dead destructures, fix exhaustive-deps warnings
description:
App.tsx (5,427 lines) currently generates 72 no-unused-vars and 70 exhaustive-deps lint warnings. This is pre-1.0 hygiene work — not a structural refactor — aimed at keeping the file readable and warning-free so contributors can trust the lint signal.

## What to do

**1. Remove or suppress unused hook destructures (lines 82–270)**
Many hooks return large objects that are fully destructured in App.tsx but most bindings are never referenced. Examples: useFileSystemExplorer returns ~12 actions (selectPath, clearExplorerSelection, expandPath, collapseAll, triggerNewFile, etc.) that are all unused; useProjectImages/useProjectAudios return addImage, removeImage, updateImageMetadata, etc., all unused; useTabManager returns ~14 bindings, almost all unused.
For each unused destructure, either:
  - Delete the binding if the value is clearly never needed (the hook side-effect is what matters), or
  - Prefix with _ if it may be wired up soon and should stay visible
Unused type imports (ClipboardState, AppSettings, StickyNote at lines 82–83) should be deleted.

**2. Fix exhaustive-deps warnings in useCallback hooks (lines 645–870)**
Most warnings are 'setActiveTabId' and 'setOpenTabs' missing from deps arrays. React setState setters are stable references — adding them to deps is correct and safe, and silences the warning without changing behavior. Fix each affected useCallback by adding the missing stable deps.

## What NOT to do

- Do not split App.tsx into modules — that is deferred to 1.0
- Do not move or rename any logic — only remove dead code and fix deps arrays
- Do not add new abstractions or hooks

## Acceptance

- npm run lint produces zero warnings in App.tsx (or a material reduction — target <10 remaining if any require judgment calls)
- npm test still passes (620/620)
- No behavioral changes
acceptance_criteria: npm run lint shows zero (or near-zero) warnings in App.tsx; npm test 620/620 passes
